README.md L306-L315:
## Exit codes

Both `check` and `metrics` share one convention:

| Code | `check` | `metrics` |
| ---- | ------- | --------- |
| `0`  | no boundary violations | no gated breach |
| `1`  | one or more imports cross a forbidden boundary | a gated breach (over-instability layer, or — under `--fail-on-violation` — an SDP or bounded-context violation) |
| `2`  | usage / config error | usage / config error |

cmd/archlint/main.go L100-L103:
	if len(violations) > 0 {
		return 1
	}
	return 0

cmd/archlint/main.go L271-L274:
	if breach {
		return 1
	}
	return 0

cmd/archlint/main.go L371-L374:
func fail(format string, args ...any) int {
	fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "archlint: "+format+"\n", args...)
	return 2
}
normalized_decision: Both commands use one exit-code contract: 0 = clean / no gated breach; 1 = check boundary violation or metrics gated breach (SDP/context/instability when gated); 2 = usage/config error. The convention enables shell/CI enforcement.
authority_evidence: README 306-315 documents shared convention; check exit 1 at main.go L100-103; metrics exit 1 at L271-274; exit 2 via fail() at L371-374
candidate_rule: exit 0 = clean / no gated breach; exit 1 = violation (check) or gated breach (metrics); exit 2 = usage/config error
